title: 'Maxxing' Named Dictionary.com's Word of the Year
paragraphs: Dictionary.com has officially chosen "maxxing" as its Word of the Year for 2026.

According to Dictionary.com, "maxxing" is short for "maximizing." It means doing something to the fullest, or improving something as much as possible. Every year, the website chooses a word that it feels reflects the experiences of the past twelve months.

The word is usually used as part of other words. One of the best-known examples is "looksmaxxing," which means trying to improve one's appearance as much as possible. However, many other versions have appeared online. For example, "tokenmaxxing" refers to using as much artificial intelligence as possible at work, and "nonnamaxxing" describes copying the habits of an Italian grandmother, or "nonna."

The word's popularity has grown very quickly over the past year. According to Steve Johnson of Dictionary Media Group, the use of "maxxing" on social media jumped by nearly 700% in the first seven months of 2026. Use of "looksmaxxing" rose by more than 1,000%. Dictionary.com also says that the word is increasingly being used on its own, and searches for "maxxing" by itself have risen sharply over the past year.

The word's origins can be traced back to the world of gaming. Dictionary.com links it to "min-maxing," a strategy in which players make their character's strengths as strong as possible to make up for its weaknesses.
Other words on Dictionary.com's shortlist this year included "affordability," "data center," "odyssey" and "unc," a slang term for someone who is considered old or out of touch.

Last year, Dictionary.com chose "67" as its Word of the Year. That choice left many people confused about what it actually meant. Johnson said that "maxxing" has had the opposite effect, since many people seem to understand it and are using it in new ways.
The choice shows how much internet culture, gaming and social media continue to shape the English language, especially among young people.
